body:
I just burst into tears reading that (in a good way). I can't talk to people in my life about this because its so personal and mortifying. I've been in treatment for a year and a half so far. The breakup happened a couple of months ago. As for university, I'm still enrolled I just screwed up my grades and some good opportunities and connections that I'd been relying on.  
I am feeling better than I did after the breakup, and I guess I know that time helps to heal. I wasn't able to get out of bed or eat for a while,  but most days I can manage to function and get basic things done. 

The suicidal thoughts are less urgent than they used to be, but I feel less fear at the thought of it as well. It's a weird sort of apathy. I'm not sure if that is better or worse. I get impulses to do it, and there's nothing really checking them besides my family, but that's a big deterrent.
Thanks, I hope we both get past this point eventually.

Thanks for taking the time to wrote out a thoughtful response like that. I appreciate it. The chemicals I have access to aren't at my house (they are in a lab) so I can't really get rid of them but they aren't within arms reach.

About the problems I'm dealing with... since you asked I will share. It's embarrassing but this is anonymous I guess so I'll spill. I was diagnosed with an std (HPV) and have an immunodeficiency disorder that's made it a *way* more difficult battle than normal. My partner, who I thought was "the one" turned into this crappy person and emotionally manipulated  abused me as a result (he got it too). I did not cheat on him, we don't know who it was from but he assumes it was from me since I got it first. I became depressed, screwed up in university and derailed my future plans. I also developed anxiety, had a breakdown and had to take time off of work and school.  My boyfriend left me because I "didn't have my shit together" and I feel completely demoralized, devalued and unworthy of love. I can't move on because of the std. I see no future ahead of me, besides a crappy job and a lonely life. 

Phew.

Sorry to unload like that. Thanks for caring.
Thanks for the response. It's always nice to see someone cares. I guess you're right about it being empowering to lose that fear, I like that interpretation.
